problem: The answer tells the student to raise the mask angle in a case where every satellite is low in the north. Raising the mask there deletes the only satellites available and makes HDOP worse. This directly contradicts Section 3 ('A high mask ... may remove spread and raise DOP') and contradicts the Q8 answer, which says a very high mask angle worsens a survey. A student writing 'raise the mask angle' in the exam would be marked down.
fix: Replace with: 'North-only directions give weak east-west strength, so HDOP is large. All satellites sitting at nearly the same low elevation also weakens the height/clock separation, so VDOP is poor. The planning step is to wait for an observation window when satellites are spread in azimuth and in elevation, and to keep the mask angle low (10°–15°) so the spread low satellites are not rejected. A high mask angle here would remove the only satellites present.'

problem: The sentence 'Low elevation raises noise and may raise VDOP' is misleading. Low elevation raises atmospheric and multipath noise, true, but it is the lack of elevation spread (all satellites at nearly the same u_z) that spoils VDOP. A low-elevation satellite mixed with high-elevation ones improves VDOP by separating height from the clock term.
fix: Write: 'Low elevation raises noise (more atmosphere and multipath). Here every satellite has almost the same low elevation, so the vertical and clock terms cannot be separated well and VDOP is also poor.'

problem: Section 1 defines the design matrix row as [-u_x, -u_y, -u_z, 1], but the worked example builds H from +u, e.g. H = [[0,1],[1,0]]. The answer is unchanged because a sign flip leaves HᵀH the same, but a student comparing the two will think one of them is wrong.
fix: Add one line: 'Rows are written here with +u instead of -u as in Section 1; the sign flip does not change HᵀH, so HDOP is the same.' Then keep H = [[0,1],[1,0]].

problem: 'DOP depends on angular spread, not height or signal strength' is ambiguous: 'height' can be read as the satellite's altitude above the ground, and elevation angle is itself part of the angular spread.
fix: Write: 'DOP depends on how the line-of-sight directions are spread, not on elevation alone, not on signal strength and not on range distance.'
